___comment_ignoreCommand: Only rebuild the frontend when something the frontend uses changed.
Every push to main used to rebuild here, including server-only commits
that produced byte-identical output — burning build quota to ship the
same bundle. Render was rebuilding the client on those same pushes too,
so a backend change built the frontend twice, once on each host.
Vercel treats exit 0 as SKIP and any non-zero as BUILD. `git diff
--quiet` exits 0 when the listed paths are unchanged, so this skips
Fail-safe by construction: on a shallow clone or first deploy HEAD^ does
not resolve, git exits non-zero, and the build RUNS. Being unsure always
means building, never silently serving a stale bundle.
`shared/` is listed because it is imported by both sides — a change
there must rebuild the frontend as well as the server. package.json and
the lockfile are listed because a dependency change alters the bundle
even when no client file was touched.
ignoreCommand: git diff --quiet HEAD^ HEAD -- client shared package.json package-lock.json vite.config.ts postcss.config.js tsconfig.json components.json vercel.json
